key_insight: The paper introduces trapdoored Clifford distributions that look like random Cliffords but can be sampled and implemented much faster when a secret trapdoor is known.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster quantum protocols that rely on random Cliffords, with potential benefits for benchmarking, classical shadows, authentication, and circuit synthesis.
method: Build a trapdoored Clifford distribution under a variant of the learning parity with noise assumption.
Design constructions with near-linear sampling/implementation and efficient tableau action on Pauli labels.
Extend the framework to trapdoored finite-field matrices and fast Clifford-related reductions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-linear-time sampling and implementation, polylogarithmic-depth realizations, and hardness results tied to worst-case matrix multiplication and batching Clifford synthesis.
watch_item: The speedups and indistinguishability guarantees rely on cryptographic assumptions, so practical deployment depends on the assumed hardness and trapdoor security.
